OpenTelemetry-based observability for AI agents, tracing model calls, tools, retrievals, tokens, cost, latency, and errors.

## Capabilities, pricing and fit

Telemetry.dev is a hosted LLM observability platform built around OpenTelemetry. It focuses on tracing AI agent runs, including model calls, tool steps, and retrievals, while normalizing reported token usage, cost, latency, and errors into inspectable traces and metrics.

Information as of September 17, 2026

### What it can do

Groups instrumented model calls, tool steps, and retrievals into traces for a request or agent run.(

Accepts traces through first-party TypeScript and Python SDKs or through a standard OTLP/HTTP exporter.(

Tracks reported input, output, cached, and reasoning tokens over time and calculates cost per call when token usage and matching model pricing are available.(

results.title: Telemetry.dev vs Traccia - AI Agents Comparison
results.content:
### Telemetry.dev

Telemetry.dev is an OpenTelemetry-based LLM observability and AI-agent tracing platform focused on collecting, normalizing, and searching traces, logs, metrics, token usage, costs, latency, and errors. It calculates model costs from reported token usage and a maintained model-pricing catalog, while allowing explicit span costs to take precedence. Its primary strength is lightweight, standards-based observability rather than broad governance or autonomous policy-control functionality. Telemetry.dev offers a free plan and paid Pro and Team plans, with pricing based primarily on monthly ingestion units, retention, projects, and seats.

Editorial ratings · 1–10, higher is better [...] Traccia is the stronger overall fit for organizations that need more than telemetry: its public positioning combines AI-agent tracing with evaluations, cost attribution, governance, policy enforcement, risk tracking, and human-review workflows. It is particularly appropriate for production environments where autonomous-agent behavior must be monitored and governed, although its broader scope and higher paid entry price can increase implementation and operating cost. Telemetry.dev is the stronger fit for teams that prioritize simple, standards-based LLM and agent observability at a low published price. Its free, Pro, and Team plans are substantially less expensive than Traccia's paid tiers, and its ingestion-unit model is straightforward for teams that can estimate telemetry volume. On the [...] Telemetry.dev is likely easier for teams seeking straightforward LLM and agent tracing. Traccia may require more initial configuration but can reduce tool sprawl for teams that also need evaluations, governance, cost attribution, and policy-oriented workflows.

### What is an AI agent

An AI agent is an application that uses a combination of LLM capabilities, tools to connect to the external world, and high-level reasoning to achieve a desired end goal or state; Alternatively, agents can also be treated as systems where LLMs dynamically direct their own processes and tool usage, maintaining control over how they accomplish tasks.

# AI Agent Monitoring: How to Observe Autonomous AI Agents in Production

#aiagents #observability #opentelemetry #llm

AI agent monitoring — also called LLM observability — is the practice of collecting, analysing, and acting on telemetry data generated by LLM calls and the autonomous agents built on top of them. Think of it as traditional APM, but purpose-built for AI workloads.

A modern AI agent is not a static API call. It's a dynamic, multi-step reasoning system that may: [...] ## OpenTelemetry: The Standard for AI Observability

OpenTelemetry (OTel) is the open-source observability framework that has become the industry standard for instrumenting distributed systems. For AI agents, it provides a vendor-neutral way to emit traces, metrics, and logs from any LLM call to any compatible backend — OpenObserve, Prometheus, Jaeger, Grafana, Datadog, and more.

The ecosystem includes dedicated auto-instrumentation libraries for all major LLM providers:

 `opentelemetry-instrumentation-openai`
 `opentelemetry-instrumentation-anthropic`
 `opentelemetry-instrumentation-langchain`
 `opentelemetry-instrumentation-llama-index`
 `opentelemetry-instrumentation-cohere` [...] ## Setting Up LLM Monitoring with OpenObserve

OpenObserve is an open-source observability platform with a native OTLP endpoint — purpose-built for high-volume telemetry at significantly lower cost and resource footprint than alternatives like the Elastic Stack.

### Prerequisites

 Python 3.8+
 `uv` package manager (or `pip`)
 An OpenObserve account — cloud or self-hosted
 Your OpenObserve organisation ID and Base64-encoded auth token
 API key for your LLM provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.)
